newsitem.title: UK: World wool textile output drops in 1995/96 season.
newsitem.headline: World wool textile output drops in 1995/96 season.

text.p: World wool processing and textile manufacturing contracted by four percent in the 1995-6 season, according to the latest review by the International Wool Textile Organisation (IWTO).
The IWTO put the decline down to de-stocking along the textile pipeline, a slow rate of recovery in consumer demand and a dramatic reduction in Chinese buying.
Combing activity fell five percent, spinning fell three percent and weaving was down by a whisker.
Worsted yarn production was down six percent, woollen yarn output down five percent and tops down three percent.
The world's wool textile industry produced a total of around 3,055,320 tonnes yarn, down almost 106,000 tonnes from the previous year.
It also produced 135 million fewer square metres of fabric at 2.02 billion square metres.
Russia saw its wool processing business cut by a fifth while Belgium, Taiwan and Japan all saw a reduction of between 15 and 17 percent in output, the report said.
Processing in the European Union as a whole fell four percent, spread evenly across the combing, spinning and weaving sectors.
Employment in combing, spinning and weaving across the globe fell 4.2 percent, slightly less than the previous season.
Portugal, the UK and France all saw significant job losses but Japan suffered the biggest cuts at nearly three thousand positions lost.
India proved a striking exception, seeing its wool textile workforce expand by 10,000 to a record 810,000.
Another bright spot was the competitiveness of wool against other fibres.
Wool increased its share of world fibre consumption to 30.8 percent from 30.5 percent the previous season while man-made fibres lost 0.2 percent, still taking 59 percent of the market.
Wool fibre posted its biggest gains against synthetics in Italy, South Korea, South Africa, Switzerland and the UK but lost out in India, Japan, Spain and the United States.
